name: Snake plant
propagation: Leaf cuttings root in water or soil, or divide rhizomes when repotting.

name: Peace lily
propagation: Divide the clump at the roots when repotting.

name: Weeping fig
propagation: Stem cuttings root in water, though success is slow.

name: Rubber plant
propagation: Stem or leaf-bud cuttings root in water or moist soil.

name: Fiddle leaf fig
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root in water.

name: Kalanchoe
propagation: Leaf or stem cuttings callus over and root in dry soil.

name: Moth orchid
propagation: Keiki (plantlets) that form on the flower spike can be potted separately.

name: Spider plant
propagation: Pot up the plantlets that form on its runners.

name: Norfolk Island pine
propagation: Grown from seed commercially; cuttings rarely keep the tree's shape.

name: Philodendron
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root readily in water.

name: Monstera
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node and an aerial root root in water.

name: Pothos
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root easily in water.

name: Heartleaf philodendron
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root readily in water.

name: Dieffenbachia
propagation: Stem cuttings or cane sections root in moist soil.

name: Dragon tree
propagation: Stem cane cuttings root in moist soil.

name: Corn plant
propagation: Stem cane cuttings root in water or moist soil.

name: Yucca
propagation: Stem cane cuttings root in soil; offsets can be divided.

name: Jade plant
propagation: Leaf or stem cuttings callus over and root in dry soil.

name: Aloe vera
propagation: Pot up the offset pups that form at the base.

name: ZZ plant
propagation: Divide the rhizome, or root a leaflet cutting (slow).

name: Christmas cactus
propagation: Stem segment cuttings callus over and root in soil.

name: Poinsettia
propagation: Softwood stem cuttings root under humidity before the latex seals the cut.

name: African violet
propagation: Leaf cuttings with the stalk root in moist soil or water.

name: Cyclamen
propagation: Grown from its tuber or from seed; dividing the tuber rarely succeeds.

name: Geranium
propagation: Stem cuttings root readily in soil.

name: Begonia
propagation: Leaf or stem cuttings root in moist soil or water.

name: Calathea
propagation: Divide the rhizome clump when repotting.

name: Prayer plant
propagation: Divide the clump, or root stem cuttings in water.

name: Kentia palm
propagation: Grown from seed; mature clumps are not easily divided at home.

name: Areca palm
propagation: Divide offshoots at the base when repotting.

name: Parlor palm
propagation: Divide offshoots at the base, or grow from seed.

name: Ponytail palm
propagation: Pot up the offset pups that form at the base of the caudex.

name: Boston fern
propagation: Divide the root clump, or pot up runners.

name: Maidenhair fern
propagation: Divide the root clump into smaller crowns.

name: English ivy
propagation: Stem cuttings root readily in water.

name: Inch plant
propagation: Stem cuttings root readily in water.

name: Croton
propagation: Stem cuttings root in water once the cut latex has sealed.

name: Anthurium
propagation: Divide the clump at the roots when repotting.

name: Chinese evergreen
propagation: Divide the clump, or root stem cuttings in water.

name: Jasmine
propagation: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings root under humidity.

name: Hibiscus
propagation: Softwood stem cuttings root under humidity.

name: Azalea
propagation: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings root in acidic, moist soil.

name: Guzmania
propagation: Pot up the offset pup that grows after the main rosette flowers.

name: Cactus
propagation: Offsets or pads root after the cut surface calluses over.

name: Echeveria
propagation: Leaf or offset cuttings callus over and root in dry soil.

name: Peperomia
propagation: Leaf or stem cuttings root in water or moist soil.

name: Pilea
propagation: Pot up the plantlets that form around the base.

name: Umbrella papyrus
propagation: Invert a cut stem's leaf top into water to root new plantlets.

name: String of pearls
propagation: Trailing stem cuttings root readily on top of soil.

name: Hoya
propagation: Stem cuttings with a node root in water or moist soil.
